service.description: For an offboarding preview and the steps of a lifecycle operation: each registered participant with what userId (an identity in the caller's scope) owns of its kind, from the owner's lookup, called as the caller (its own permission applies): participantList, each {participantKey, ownerApp, title, resourceKind, state (ready, unavailable: the caller lacks the owner's permission, failed: the lookup failed, named without its diagnostics), resourceList, pauses}; and participantSteps, the steps mantle.party.IdentityServices.start#Lifecycle takes (a pause per participant that has one, a transfer per resource). A registration naming a missing service, or one without the owned-resource contract, is logged by name and left out. Needs ADMIN_IDENTITY_VIEW.

TransferOwnership (design §4 LifecycleDetail): a step waiting for a new owner, or failed, handed to toUserId, a staff identity in the caller's scope that is enabled: the step's service and resource parameter must be what its participant registered (NOT_REGISTERED otherwise), then Mantle's retry#LifecycleStep calls the owner's transfer service, which checks its own permission and whether toUserId may own the resource. Answers retry#LifecycleStep's outcome (a refusal as a reason). Needs ADMIN_IDENTITY_MANAGE.

Projects' participant lookup: the open assignments of userId's party, counted by kind (tasks: open Commons tasks outside a project; workItems: open tasks of a project; requests: open requests it is the assignee of), each a resource {resourceId (the kind), resourceName, resourceKind assignment, transferable, note}; counts only, never a task's name. The caller's own, or an identity in the caller's scope with ADMIN_IDENTITY_VIEW.

Projects' participant transfer: the open assignments of one kind (assignmentKind tasks, workItems or requests) of fromUserId's party reassigned to toUserId's, each through its owner's service as the caller (ironstone.commons.TaskServices.reassign#Task, ironstone.projects.WorkItemServices.bulk#WorkItems assign, ironstone.commons.RequestServices.reassign#Request), which decide who may reassign it; each on its own, the ones refused counted and the first reason named (an error, so the step stays to be retried for the rest). The caller's own, or an identity in the caller's scope with ADMIN_IDENTITY_MANAGE.
